input.rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the federal and state courts in New York City, and no arbitration clause — this is our preferred position.

input.quote: Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent.
input.rationale: Assignment is blanket-prohibited for Licensee with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, and Article XX makes the Agreement terminate automatically on our change of control (with a right of first refusal over our own M&A in Article XXII). Both are walk-away items; we added the affiliate/successor carve-out and removed the change-of-control termination trigger.

input.quote: ARTICLE III OWNERSHIP Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.
input.rationale: Licensor owning its platform is acceptable, but the Agreement gives us no ownership of, or lasting licence to, customisations and front-end development we pay for under Article VII(b), and it is silent on our own data (which the broad Confidential Information definition and the five-day return obligation could sweep up). That falls short of the fallback perpetual, irrevocable licence, so we added a Licensee Data ownership sentence and a licence-back for Licensee-funded deliverables.

input.quote: grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below
input.rationale: The grant runs to Licensee alone; affiliates and contractors are excluded (use is limited to Licensee employees and outsourcing/service-bureau use is barred), it is non-transferable, and the licence can be revoked immediately for any breach with no notice or cure. That fails the fallback (affiliates on notice, transfer to a successor, revocation only for uncured material breach), so we extended the grant and added a cure period.
